title: Any signed-in citizen can learn whether a mobile number belongs to a registered account: the mobile-OTP request answers 409 "already registered to another account" for a used number and 200 for a free one
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-sec/mobile-oracle.mjs (citizenB asks about citizenA's number, read in-script, and a random number)
root_cause: the duplicate check runs before anything and its answer is returned as is; no rate limit on the route other than the per-number OTP cooldown, so a list of numbers can be tested one by one (each new number gets its own cooldown).

title: Mobile "verification" never involves the mobile: the code goes to the account's e-mail, so any citizen can get any number (a neighbour's) marked Verified and block its real owner (409 for them afterwards)
repro: as citizenB POST /api/profile/mobile-otp/request {mobileNumber:<any 10-digit number>} -> 200 OTP sent; the code is mailed to citizenB's own e-mail ([mailer] log line "Verify your mobile number"); POST /verify with it marks that number Verified on citizenB's profile
root_cause: the OTP is e-mailed instead of sent by SMS to the number being verified; the profile page then shows a green Verified chip (profile/page.tsx:491) for a number nobody proved they hold.

title: PUT /api/profile changes the mobile number with no OTP and no duplicate check, and keeps mobile_verified TRUE, so the Verified chip then stands on a number never checked
repro: after a verified number, PUT /api/profile with the usual fields and a different mobileNumber; GET /api/profile shows the new number with mobileVerified true
root_cause: mobileNumber left in profileUpdateSchema and the UPDATE; the verified flag is not tied to the number it verified.

area: personal data in logs / honest status
title: With SMTP off, every OTP mail writes the account's e-mail address into the server log, and the mobile-OTP route still answers "OTP sent."
root_cause: sendMail logs the recipient address; the route ignores sendMail's {ok:false, reason:"not_configured"} (mailer.ts says callers must not claim a mail was sent unless ok).

title: Forgot-password tells a registered e-mail from an unknown one, against its own comment: a second request answers with cooldownRemaining only for a real account, and the first takes ~20x longer
root_cause: the generic message is kept but the cooldown field and the OTP hashing/sending happen only for an existing account. (POST /api/auth/register also answers 409 "An account with this email already exists.", register/route.ts:44, so the address space leaks there too.)
where: src/app/api/auth/forgot-password/request-otp/route.ts:35-41 (cooldownRemaining only on the exists branch; bcrypt + mail only there)

title: A citizen's profile photo is written under public/ with a guessable name (user-<id>-<ms>.png): on the running production server it is a 404, so the photo never shows; once the server restarts it is served to anyone with no sign-in
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-sec/photo.mjs (citizenB uploads a 1x1 PNG, then the returned path is fetched with no cookie)
root_cause: profile photos use the old public-folder pattern that complaint media moved away from (complaint-media.ts keeps files private and serves them through an auth-checked route). next start does not serve files added to public/ after start, and serves them with no check after a restart; the name is the sequential user id plus a millisecond timestamp. Note: citizenB's profile_photo now points at that 404 path.

title: Change-password checks the current password with no limit: a stolen session cookie can guess the account password ~20 times a second, around the sign-in limit (8 per 15 min) and the step-up limit (5 per 15 min)
repro: node tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/hunt2-sec/cp-guess.mjs (12 random wrong current passwords with one citizenB session; nothing is changed)
root_cause: the route has no failure counter (factors.ts verifyFactor has one: confirm-fail:<user>, 5 per 15 min). For a staff account the guessed password then passes the "Confirm it's you" step-up meant to stop a stolen cookie from sending e-mail, exporting or deciding, and a hit changes the password and signs every other device out (revokeSessions), locking the owner out.

title: "Sign out other sessions" needs no confirmation: whoever holds a copied staff cookie can end the owner's sessions and keep a fresh 12-hour one for themselves
repro: code path: POST /api/auth/security {action:"signout_others"} with any staff session cookie; every other session of the account is revoked and the caller gets a new cookie with the new token version
root_cause: signout_others is the recovery action for a stolen session, but it trusts the session it is meant to recover from; it should ask for the password or an e-mailed code first.
where: src/app/api/auth/security/route.ts:47-52 (signout_others: revokeSessions + new cookie, no requireConfirm)

title: Filing a complaint has no rate limit: a signed-in citizen can file without end, each one a paid classifier call (when a model key is set), a dataset append and a case on a department's list; its JSON body is also read with no size cap
repro: code path: grep checkRateLimit src/app/api/complaints/route.ts finds nothing; vary the title per request and every POST files a new complaint
root_cause: the duplicate guard was added for double clicks, not for volume; no per-citizen or per-IP limit on filings.
where: src/app/api/complaints/route.ts:47 (req.json() uncapped), 54-63 (only a one-at-a-time lock and a same-text-just-filed check), 191 (classifyComplaint per filing)

title: Six unit tests mix SQLite own clock (datetime(now) in the test schema) with the app JS clock, so they fail whenever the process clock is moved (future-clock runs): they cannot check those paths for date time bombs
repro: QA_FROZEN_NOW=<+30d> QA_CLOCK_TICKING=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--require tests/qa/pass4/freeze-clock.cjs node tests/qa/pass6/suite.mjs --tag future-30
failing_test: src/lib/manu/manu.sqlite.test.ts (4), src/lib/manu/sms.pass5.test.ts (1), src/app/api/collector/decisions/route.sqlite.test.ts (1) under a moved clock
root_cause: test schemas use DEFAULT (datetime(now,+330 minutes)) and inserts with SQLite datetime(now): SQLite reads the wall clock while the store dialect NOW() reads JS Date; in production both are the wall clock, so this is a test-harness limit, not a product bug

title: The mailer writes the recipient's e-mail address into the server log on every failed or unconfigured send
repro: Code: console.warn(`[mailer] SMTP is not configured; no email sent to ${to} (${subject})`) and console.error(`[mailer] Failed to send "${subject}" to ${to}: ${detail}`).

title: Registered e-mails can be told apart: sign-in skips bcrypt for unknown e-mails and answers 'deactivated' before the password check; register answers 409; reset returns cooldownRemaining only for real accounts
repro: Code path (not run live: it would spend the shared per-e-mail sign-in allowance). Unknown e-mail: 401 at once; known e-mail: bcrypt.compare first (tens of ms); deactivated account: 403 'This account has been deactivated.' with any password; a second reset request for a real account inside the cooldown carries cooldownRemaining.
root_cause: The generic-message rule covers the reset text but not timing, the deactivated branch, registration or the cooldown field. Citizens' e-mail addresses are personal data.

title: A tab copy (/api/auth/tab) and the legacy-cookie move re-set a staff session cookie with the citizen's 7-day Max-Age; the JWT inside still ends at 12 h, so the session does not outlive it, but the cookie lingers

root_cause: The tab copy keeps the token but not its length; harmless for access (exp is checked) but the cookie's Max-Age disagrees with the session.
where: src/lib/auth.ts:158 and :176 (setSessionCookie(..., token) with the default SESSION_MAX_AGE, src/lib/session-cookies.ts:43)
